headline: Seven banks have arranged a further US$3.7 billion (RM15 billion) of financing for DayOne, the Singapore-based data center company, to expand its Johor campus in Malaysia, doubling its financing there to RM30 billion.
score_reason: Fresh, confirmed by a joint lender statement and several outlets; a financing deal, not a build milestone.
importance_line: It shows banks still lend heavily for AI data center building in Southeast Asia, which matters to Johor's economy and power grid and to DayOne's planned US listing, but it says nothing about how fast the capacity will be used.
summary: The Business Times reports, citing a joint statement from the seven lenders (CIMB, Credit Agricole CIB, DBS, Maybank, OCBC, Standard Chartered and UOB), that they have arranged RM15 billion (US$3.7 billion) of new financing for DayOne's data centre campus in Johor, Malaysia, which with RM15 billion arranged in 2025 brings DayOne's financing there to RM30 billion. DayOne, a Singapore-based data centre company, filed on 6 Oct 2026 for a US stock-market listing that would raise up to US$5 billion at a possible US$20 billion valuation.
